The nightly job no longer counts a retried payment twice. The fix is committed on `main` as `6d0ac1f`, with a follow-up commit `5516d6e` that fills in the fix record.

**The bug:** `ReconciliationWorker.run` in `src/orders-api/reconciliation_worker.py` counted every payment row and never looked at the payment id, so a retry with the same id was counted once per arrival.

**The fix:** the worker now keeps a set of payment ids it has already seen and skips repeats before the order-match check. I added a test, `test_a_retried_payment_counts_once`, which failed with `2 != 1` before the change. The full suite now passes: 9 tests, all OK.

**Things to know:**
- **Same defect in the audit copy.** `src/orders-service-v1/nightly_job.py` has the same double count. I left it alone because that copy is read-only for audits and a hook refuses edits to it. It needs fixing if anyone still runs it.
- **Assumption.** I assumed a payment id is unique per payment, so two rows with one id are the same payment. If the bank can reuse ids, this fix would undercount.
- **Repository state.** There is no git remote, so there is no pull request. `README.md` (already modified) and `notes/` (untracked) were not part of this change and are untouched.
- **Workspace gaps.** `tools/symbols.py` and `workspace.json` are not in this checkout, so I used grep. The playbook's defect register (`docs/records/defects.md`) doesn't exist either, so the audit-copy defect is noted in the fix record instead.

The fix record is at `docs/records/fixes/2026-11-24-duplicate-retried-payments.md`.
